meta.title: RifAccess — Measuring rural isolation in the Rif
meta.description: RifAccess measures how douars in the Rif reach all-season roads, healthcare and schools to clarify investment priorities.

hero.title: Measuring rural isolation in the Rif.
hero.promise: RifAccess identifies isolated douars, measures their access to essential services, and helps reveal where investment can open them up first.

diagram.title: One road. One radius. A reality that changes with the season.
diagram.svgTitle: Diagram of douar access to an all-season road
diagram.svgDesc: A road crosses the territory. A band represents a two-kilometre distance. Accessible douars are green and isolated douars are terracotta. During the rainy season two tracks disappear and two douars become isolated.
diagram.dryStatus: Tracks complete the network during the dry season.
diagram.rainyStatus: Impassable tracks are removed from the network.

figures.populationLabel: rural inhabitants in the region — RGPH 2024
figures.douarsLabel: douars in the HCP RGPH 2024 database

problem.body: In the Rif, straight-line proximity does not tell the whole story. Terrain, dispersed settlement, and tracks that become impassable in the rain turn a few kilometres into uncertain travel time.
problem.noteRain: A track can connect in the dry season and cut off in the rains.
problem.noteServices: Isolation is visible in access to healthcare and school.

measures.title: Four readings of the same territory.
measures.intro: Distance alone is not enough. We combine the road network, terrain, seasonality and population to make isolation legible.
measures.formulaNumerator: rural population within 2 km of an all-season road
measures.raiBody: The share of rural people living within 2 km of an all-season road, in line with SDG indicator 9.1.1.
measures.timeBody: The journey to the nearest health centre and school, including the effect of slope.
measures.seasonBody: The change in access between the dry and rainy seasons when unpaved tracks leave the network.
measures.priorityBody: A combined reading of population and isolation to identify interventions to examine first.

method.title: From a point on the map to a territorial priority.
method.intro: A reproducible seven-step path, from raw sources to a reading designed for decisions.

steps.title: Collection
steps.description: Gather territorial, road, topographic and demographic datasets.

steps.title: Preparation
steps.description: Harmonise formats, reference systems and geographic quality.

steps.title: All-season network
steps.description: Classify roads and distinguish rain-sensitive tracks.

steps.title: RAI calculation
steps.description: Apply the 2 km threshold around the all-season network.

steps.title: Travel time
steps.description: Model trips to health and school with the effect of slope.

steps.title: Validation
steps.description: Check results and document the method's limitations.

steps.title: Priorities
steps.description: Combine population and isolation into a prioritisation view.

data.title: Official sources, enriched by digital terrain evidence.
data.intro: HCP data provides the territorial backbone. Open and non-conventional sources describe the network, terrain and accessibility.

territory.title: Four provinces, one access challenge.
territory.body: The study covers Al Hoceima, Chefchaouen, Ouezzane and Tétouan in the Tanger–Tétouan–Al Hoceima region.
territory.note: Schematic map with no administrative boundary value. No provincial indicator has been fabricated at this stage.
territory.mapTitle: Schematic map of the four provinces studied
territory.mapDesc: Four adjacent shapes represent Tétouan, Chefchaouen, Ouezzane and Al Hoceima.
